classification.difficultyReason: Apply the two taught PDF conditions and evaluate straightforward definite integrals.

content.prompt: Which of the following functions describe continuous probability distributions?

answer.worked:
$f(x)=0.2\geq0$ throughout $[1,6]$.
$$\begin{align*}\int_1^6 0.2\,dx&=0.2(6-1)\\&=0.2(5)\\&=1\end{align*}$$
Both conditions hold, so this is a valid PDF.

answer.short: Not a PDF; the integral is $\frac32\ne1$.
answer.worked:
$f(x)=\frac{x}{12}\geq0$ throughout $[0,6]$.
$$\begin{align*}\int_0^6\frac{x}{12}\,dx&=\left[\frac{x^2}{24}\right]_0^6\\&=\frac{36}{24}-0\\&=\frac32\ne1\end{align*}$$
The total area is not $1$, so this is not a PDF.

answer.short: Not a PDF; the integral is $\frac1{16}\ne1$.
answer.worked:
$f(x)=\frac{x^3}{324}\geq0$ throughout $[0,3]$.
$$\begin{align*}\int_0^3\frac{x^3}{324}\,dx&=\left[\frac{x^4}{1296}\right]_0^3\\&=\frac{81}{1296}-0\\&=\frac1{16}\ne1\end{align*}$$
The total area is not $1$, so this is not a PDF.

$f(x)=\frac{x^2}{21}\geq0$ throughout $[1,4]$.
$$\begin{align*}\int_1^4\frac{x^2}{21}\,dx&=\left[\frac{x^3}{63}\right]_1^4\\&=\frac{64}{63}-\frac1{63}\\&=\frac{63}{63}\\&=1\end{align*}$$
Both conditions hold, so this is a valid PDF.
